jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Spanish, Tenure Track, Fall 2027
jobs.institution: Chapman University: World Languages and Cultures
jobs.description:
Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences at Chapman University invites applications for a tenure track assistant professor of Spanish, who possesses native or near-native fluency in Spanish, within the Department of World Languages and Cultures, effective August 2027.
Chapman University is a nationally ranked, R2 Carnegie Classified, private institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California’s most diverse and vibrant regions. Chapman’s campuses are home to nearly 10,000 students representing 50 states, 4 territories, and 76 countries. The 11 schools and colleges of Chapman, including Wilkinson College, offer 50 bachelors, 29 masters, and 8 doctoral programs, along with nearly 75 minors and 19 accelerated and bridge programs. Classes are taught by the more than 1,100 dedicated faculty members who are leaders in their fields, including Nobel Prize recipients, MacArthur Fellows, National Medal of Science honorees, former U.S. Supreme Court clerks, and Emmy, Grammy, and Academy Award winners.
The mission of Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences is to foster rigorous inquiry among our students through a curriculum grounded in the liberal arts that is scholarly, creative, interdisciplinary, and experiential. Wilkinson College plays an important and unique role in the educational journey of every Chapman student and aims to ensure that graduates are prepared to assume their responsibility as global citizens, acting knowledgeably, and providing compassionate leadership in our community and world. The Spanish program is dedicated to teaching Spanish language, literature, and culture through technology, innovative methods, and interdisciplinary approaches.
Responsibilities
Maintain an active program of scholarly research and publication appropriate to the candidate’s field.
Teach lower-division Spanish language courses at multiple levels of proficiency.
Develop and teach innovative upper-division courses that complement and expand the existing Spanish curriculum.
Contribute to the development of an innovative undergraduate program
Advise and mentor undergraduate students.
Engage broader interdisciplinary conversations within the Department of World Languages and Cultures through teaching, research, and curricular development.
Tenure-track faculty are expected to develop and maintain an active research agenda for future tenure consideration and are evaluated on their research/scholarly activity, teaching and service.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, WOT – Pediatric Surgeon, University of Washington and Seattle Children’s Hospital
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Surgery
jobs.description:
Seattle Children’s Hospital and the Department of Surgery, Division of Pediatric General Surgery at the University of Washington invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the ranks of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor without tenure (WOT), by reason of funding with an anticipated start date of January 2027. The successful candidate will be expected to support the department's commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. Assistant Professors WOT are eligible for multi-year appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July 1 – June 30). Associate Professors WOT and Professors WOT hold indefinite appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July-June). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off.
Commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination, the base salary range for this position will be:
Assistant Professor, $35,417-$39,584 ($425,004 - $475,008 annually)
Associate Professor, $41,667-$50,000 ($500,004 - $600,000 annually)
Professor $52,084-$56,250 ($625,008 - $675,000 annually)
The successful candidate will be expected to provide the full spectrum of general surgical care and surgical oncology care for pediatric patients. including developing and leading our surgical oncology team. Pediatric General Surgery at Seattle Children’s Hospital consists of 16 board-certified pediatric surgeons and supports a busy tertiary care hospital practice in addition to regional clinics. This practice may include a significant commitment to laboratory research or clinical outcomes research related to surgical oncology. The successful candidate may pursue extramural funding with emphasis on federal grant submissions regarding bench or outcomes research related to the individual’s clinical practice. The successful candidate will be given adequate protected time to develop academic endeavors. Excellent clinical epidemiologic and basic science research resources are available, including opportunity for involvement with the Seattle Children’s Institute for Research (SCIR), the Department of Surgery Division of Research, as well as the Department of Surgery Surgical Outcome Research Center (SORCE). All University of Washington faculty engage in teaching, research, and service.

jobs.description:
The Joukowsky Institute for Archaeology and the Ancient World (JIAAW) at Brown University invites applications for the position of Postdoctoral Research Associate in Archaeology and the Ancient World. Exceptional junior scholars who can contribute to the diversity and excellence of the academic community through their research, teaching, and service are encouraged to apply. Multiple Postdoctoral Research Associate positions will be filled.
We seek candidates who have demonstrated a capacity for innovative research, engaged scholarship, and cross-disciplinary thinking. Geographic area is open, though some preference will be given to scholars who work on the archaeology of the Mediterranean, Egypt, and/or surrounding regions of the Middle East and North Africa. While the boundaries of the search are flexible, we are especially interested in applicants who demonstrate shared or complementary methodological expertise, geographic/temporal focus, theoretical interests, and/or potential research collaborations with one or more JIAAW Academic Faculty members.

Teaching may be at both the undergraduate and graduate levels; interdisciplinary offerings are desirable. Historically, successful postdocs have advanced the mission of JIAAW not only through their research and teaching, but by organizing reading or working groups, organizing small conferences, inviting speakers, and initiating new interdisciplinary or community connections.

For this position, Brown offers only the J-1 visa classification to scholars who need immigration sponsorship in order to enter the U.S. and commence lawful employment under the terms of their appointment.

jobs.institution: University of Washington: Philosophy
jobs.description:
The Department of Philosophy at the University of Washington, Seattle invites applications for a full-time (100% FTE) faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor Tenure-Track, with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community.
The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time basis for a 9-month academic tenure-track appointment, 3-year term, renewable, beginning September 16, 2027.
The base salary range for this position will be $9,750-13,000 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
Area of Specialization (AOS): AI and Philosophy. Area of Concentration (AOC): Open, but we are particularly interested in candidates who can add to our strengths in applied ethics or philosophy of science.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to and develop a curriculum that speaks to undergraduate students across campus, including students in Arts & Sciences, Computer Science, and Engineering.
The UW Department of Philosophy is a vibrant community of philosophers committed to excellence in research and teaching. With an expansive vision and an outward focus, the department aspires to practice engaged philosophy, believing our discipline has vital contributions to offer all areas of inquiry. We aim to foster inclusive and interdisciplinary conversations in which philosophical tools and methods are brought to bear upon problems and topics of public interest. Individuals whose backgrounds and interests align with these commitments, including members of groups traditionally underrepresented in our field, are strongly encouraged to apply.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service.

jobs.title: 2027 Computer Science Assistant Professor/Associate Professor
jobs.institution: Wenzhou-Kean University: Computer Science
jobs.description:
Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education.
WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University.
In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master’s and 3 doctorate programs. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions.
Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China’s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai.
About the Job:
The College of Science, Mathematics, and Technology is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the computer science department at WKU.
All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the start of the 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review.
A Tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor is a full-time, 10-month employee who teaches 24 credits per academic year. Tenure-track faculty normally teach 2 different courses, with each section typically consisting of 24-30 students. Faculty is required to conduct research, provide high quality teaching and provide service to the university and/or professional community. Six credits teaching release time will be provided to new faculty each year for the first three consecutive years of the appointment to support external research grant development and other significant research endeavors. Thereafter, release time may be available by application on a competitive basis. The university will provide start-up grants (up to 300,000 RMB) in support of their research programs. After joining WKU, faculty will apply to a variety of internal research funds and external grants at the municipal, provincial, and national levels. Faculty members successfully obtaining eligible external grants will be afforded release time ranging from 3-12 credits per year.
Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening, and online courses. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach interdisciplinary support courses.

The Department of Neurology at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the non-tenure academic clinician track. Applicants must have an M.D. or M.D./Ph.D. or equivalent degree. Candidates must be board-certified in Neurology, must have completed an ACGME- approved or UCNS-approved fellowship in Neurocritical Care, and must be board-certified or eligible in Neurocritical Care.
Teaching responsibilities may include teaching of fellows, residents, advanced practice providers and medical students will be expected through bedside rounds and through a formal didactic curriculum, including the Division’s neurocritical care didactic conference. Teaching in the Perelman School of Medicine through formal courses, such as the Brain and Behavior Course, will be strongly encouraged. Opportunities for educational leadership within the Penn Neurocritical Care Fellowship Program may be available to the right candidate.
Clinical responsibilities may include for this primarily clinical position, responsibilities will include attending on all services of the Neurocritical Care Division, which presently include the primary inpatient NeuroICU services at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania (HUP) and Penn Presbyterian Medical Center (PPMC), inpatient neurocritical care consultation, including consultation for the RECOVER (Recovery Following Acute Brain Injury) Program at HUP and/or PPMC. Outpatient responsibilities, most likely in the RECOVER Program clinic or the TBI clinic, are anticipated; the specific balance of inpatient consultative and outpatient work will be tailored to the applicant’s interests. The position might, at a later date, include a Neurocritical Care Consult Service and/or a Tele-neurocritical care consult service.
The applicant must have demonstrated excellent qualifications in education and clinical care. The successful applicant will have experience in the field of Neurology with completion of a fellowship in Neurocritical care.

jobs.title: Tenured/Tenure-Track: Open Rank & Title
jobs.institution: Texas A&M University: College of Architecture
jobs.description:
The College of Architecture at Texas A&M University invites applications for 3 full-time tenured/tenure-track positions at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor in AI-Powered Planning, Design, and Construction (AI-PDC) with 9-month academic appointments to begin in Fall 2027. Each selected candidate's home department will be determined based on their expertise, preference, and departmental/college priorities. The College has three departments, including Architecture, Construction Science, Landscape Architecture & Urban Planning.
These faculty cluster hires, together with existing faculty, will lead Texas A&M University’s College of Architecture to become the world's leading land-grant college for AI in the built environment, advancing the responsible development and application of AI to plan, design, build, and sustain communities that are safe, healthy, prosperous, and environmentally responsible.
Through interdisciplinary research, professional education, and public engagement, we will shape how AI transforms the professions of architecture, landscape architecture, urban planning, land development, and construction. Our work will ensure that AI serves people and communities by enhancing human creativity, improving decision-making, expanding access to opportunities, strengthening infrastructure and housing systems, advancing environmental stewardship, and preparing the next generation of built environment leaders. Drawing on Texas A&M's land-grant mission, we will develop AI solutions that address real-world challenges facing communities, industries, and governments, while critically examining the societal, ethical, environmental, and economic impacts of AI itself.
The ideal candidates will have backgrounds in the disciplines represented in the College, as well as advanced knowledge of AI technologies and its applications in research, teaching, service, and/or practice across the planning, design, and construction disciplines. We are seeking candidates who bring innovative, interdisciplinary, and critical ideas and approaches to strategically grow the College’s position as a global leader in AI research, creative work, and education related to the built environment.
For this search, AI is broadly understood to include machine learning, generative AI, agentic systems, multimodal AI, and related approaches. These approaches may draw on text, imagery, spatial data, building information modeling (BIM), simulation, digital twins, and other sources of data and knowledge.
We welcome research that develops AI methods, advances their applications, or critically examines their implications for the built and natural environments. Potential areas of specialization are listed below. Candidates are expected to specialize in one or more areas; expertise across all areas is neither required nor expected.
AI for Planning, Design, and Construction Decision Support: Development of methodologies and applications of AI to spatial analysis, forecasting, scenario development, visualization across the planning, design, and construction processes.
AI for Sustainable, Resilient, and Healthy Communities: Use of AI to support climate adaptation, hazard mitigation, housing, infrastructure, environmental stewardship, resource management, and community well-being.
Human-Centered, Ethical, and Equitable AI: Research on governance, policy, professional practice, public engagement, transparency, ethics, equity, trust, and the societal implications of AI.
Intelligent Buildings, Infrastructure, and Construction Systems: AI-enabled research in structural and architectural engineering, advanced construction materials, infrastructure and construction management, robotics and automation, sensing and monitoring, safety, building energy and performance, resilience, and lifecycle management.
AI for the Environment and Resource Systems: Research on the environmental footprint of AI, including data centers, energy demand, water use, land use, carbon impacts, and strategies to enhance sustainability and resilience.
Education, Workforce Development, and the Future of Professional Practice: Applications of AI in education, professional training, workforce development, and the evolving roles of built environment professionals.
Successful candidates will be expected to build a visible research program around AI, work across disciplines both within and outside the College, teach AI-related courses, advise graduate students, develop new curriculum related to AI, serve as thought leaders on AI’s impacts on the built environment, and help shape the College’s strategic identity as it relates to AI.
About the College and University:
The College of Architecture at Texas A&M University is one of the nation’s largest and most comprehensive colleges focused on the built environment. With three academic departments and six research centers, the college serves more than 3,200 students across 14 degree programs with 220 faculty and staff dedicated to advancing education and research to plan, design, and build a better world. To learn more about the College of Architecture, visit www.arch.tamu.edu.
Founded in 1876, Texas A&M University is the oldest public institution of higher education in Texas and one of the largest universities in the United States. With one of the largest university endowments in the nation, Texas A&M ranks among the nation’s leading public universities in annual research expenditures. Texas A&M students are known for their strong engagement with the university and the local community. Our programs and traditions create a culture in which the university’s core values of respect, leadership, integrity, loyalty, excellence, and selfless service are embodied by its students, faculty, staff, and alumni.
Texas A&M University's VISION Supercomputer is a $45 million NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD located at the West Campus Data Center in College Station, ranked as the most powerful academic supercomputer in the United States. The VISION Supercomputer, as well as the TAMU High-Performance Research Computing facility, support A&M research initiatives in key areas, including those aligned with the planning, design, and construction disciplines, such as Generative AI applications, image processing, graphics rendering, scientific simulations, robotics enablement, among others.
About the Bryan-College Station Area:
The Bryan–College Station area offers a high quality of life at a relatively low cost of living with the convenience of a growing metropolitan area. The community combines a small town feel with a broad range of cultural, recreational, dining, and entertainment amenities for individuals and families. The area features more than 90 public parks, Lake Bryan, live music and community events, museums, and a variety of locally owned restaurants, shops, and attractions. Located in the center of the Texas Triangle, Bryan–College Station is within driving distance of Houston, Dallas–Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio, and the Gulf Coast.
For faculty in the built environment disciplines, the region offers a meaningful setting to engage in pressing questions about climate resilience, natural hazards, transportation, demographic change, and economic development. These issues are central to the future of Texas and increasingly relevant nationwide, creating strong opportunities for impactful teaching, research, and service.

jobs.title: Post Doctoral Associate
jobs.institution: New York University: Computer Science & Engineering
jobs.description:
POSTDOCTORAL ASSOCIATE
New York University Tandon School of Engineering
The Visualization Imaging and Data Analysis Center (VIDA) at New York University invites applications for a Postdoctoral Associate. The successful candidate will join a research group working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, data management, visualization, and scientific discovery, with a focus on developing AI-driven methods and open-source systems to address challenges in data discovery, integration, and agentic systems.
New York University (NYU) is a top private university in the United States, and the Tandon School of Engineering, located in Brooklyn, NY, is deeply committed to excellence in research, teaching, and learning. Tandon fosters innovation and entrepreneurship that make a difference in the world. VIDA offers a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment with strong connections to NYU's broader strengths in AI/ML and partnerships spanning the natural sciences and biomedical research. New York City provides unmatched access to world-class academic institutions, leading industry research laboratories, and a thriving startup ecosystem — making it an exceptional setting for postdoctoral career development.
Responsibilities
The candidate will help lead new research efforts, contribute to ongoing projects, and be a core member of VIDA, including mentoring Ph.D. and MS student researchers as appropriate.
Conduct original research on AI-driven methods for discovery, integration, and agentic systems
Design and implement open-source tools and systems
Publish and present research at leading venues
Pursue independent collaborations across disciplines
Participate in teaching and mentorship
Salary range
The position comes with a competitive salary, full benefits, and strong support for career development, including teaching opportunities for those who wish to pursue them. The initial appointment is for two years, with the possibility of an extension. In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $75,000 – $110,000.

jobs.title: Associate Research Scientist
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Systems Biology
jobs.description: The Wang Lab in the Department of Systems Biology at Columbia Univeristy Irving Medical Center is looking for a full-time Associate Research Scientist to join the team. The Associate Research Scientist will conduct research in synthetic biology and microbiome engineering, with a focus on engineering gut microbes and microbial communities for therapeutic applications. The position will involve developing and applying genetic and molecular tools to program bacteria to detect disease-associated signals, deliver therapeutic molecules, and modify microbial activities and host–microbe interactions in the gastrointestinal tract. Research will explore applications in inflammatory bowel disease, metabolic disorders, and other conditions influenced by the gut microbiome. The researcher will design and execute experiments, analyze and interpret data, develop new methods and technologies, prepare manuscripts and research presentations, and contribute to collaborative projects within the laboratory. Research activities may include microbial genome editing, synthetic gene circuit design, direct engineering of resident gut bacteria, and evaluation of engineered microbial functions in laboratory and preclinical models. The position will also involve investigating the stability, specificity, and safety of engineered microbes and their ability to function within complex gut communities, with the goal of developing new approaches to prevent and treat disease.

jobs.title: 2027 Biology Tenure Track Assistant/Associate Professor
jobs.institution: Wenzhou-Kean University: Biology
jobs.description:
Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education.
WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University.
In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master’s and 3 doctorate programs. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions.
Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China’s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai.
About the Job:
The College of Science, Mathematics and Technology is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the biology department at WKU.
All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the start of the 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review.
Tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor is a full-time, 10-month employee who teaches 24 credits per academic year. Tenure-track faculty normally teach 2 different courses, with each section typically consisting of 24-30 students. Faculty are required to conduct research, provide high-quality teaching, and provide service to the university and/or professional community. Six credits of teaching release time will be provided to new faculty each year for the first three consecutive years of the appointment to support external research grant development and other significant research endeavors. Thereafter, release time may be available by application on a competitive basis. The university will provide start-up grants (up to 300,000 RMB) supporting their research programs. After joining WKU, faculty will apply for external grants at the municipal, provincial, and national levels. Faculty members successfully obtaining eligible external grants will be afforded release time ranging from 3-12 credits per year.
Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening, and online courses. Interest in or experience with advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty are required to teach General Education courses as needed, and must be able to teach wet‑lab courses at either introductory or advanced levels. Opportunities are also available to teach interdisciplinary support courses.

jobs.title: Teaching Associate: Instructor for Introduction to R Course
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Evans School of Public Policy & Governance
jobs.description:
The Evans School of Public Policy & Governance at the University of Washington invites applications for a Teaching Associate position to teach a one-quarter course in the 2026-2027 academic year. Teaching Associates are quarterly faculty who may be rehired based on programmatic need. We anticipate instructional need for Winter Quarter (December 16 – March 15) and Spring Quarter (March 16-June 15). Applicants may be considered for one or both of these quarterly appointments. We seek applicants who will demonstrate commitment to excellence in teaching in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate will join our faculty on a quarterly basis at 20.83% - 24.39% FTE commensurate with instructional assignment.
The per-course compensation for this one-quarter, 2-credit course will be $5,000. The full-time monthly base salary range for this position will be $ 6,833 – 8,000 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. Please note: this is a less than full-time appointment so the salary range will be prorated commensurate with assigned FTE.
For this initial appointment we seek a candidate to teach a 2-credit course, PUBPOL 598: Introduction to R, , intended for Master of Public Administration (MPA) students and other UW graduate students. The course is designed to familiarize students with the R environment for statistical computing. Students in the course will gain experience organizing, managing, cleaning, and merging complex social science data; writing basic R functions; and producing clear, replicable analyses and visualizations. The course will emphasize workflows that support transparency and efficiency in empirical research and prepare students to integrate R within other Evans School courses.
A Teaching Associate instructing PUBPOL 598 is expected to:
Develop a syllabus and Canvas page for the course.
Teach a 50-minute course twice weekly on the UW Seattle campus.
Develop in-class learning activities and modest homework assignments to facilitate learning.
Bring real-world, applied examples into the classroom from a range of social science and public policy contexts.
Review, assess, and provide feedback on student work in a timely manner.
Be available, through office hours and one-on-one appointments, to meet with students to answer questions and support their learning.
Collaborate with Evans School faculty and staff as needed in the development of course learning outcomes and content; meet with the Associate Dean as needed to review instructional performance.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: The Polytechnic School
jobs.description:
The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering at Arizona State University (ASU) and The Polytechnic School seek applicants for a Postdoctoral Research Scholar position on an engineering education research project under the supervision of Dr. Dina Verdín. The postdoctoral research scholar will contribute to an NSF research project titled Toward Curricular Integration Leveraging Students’ Community Cultural Wealth in an Engineering Design Context (Award# 2603157).
The project advances asset-based engineering education research by extending Community Cultural Wealth to engineering design-based courses and by developing a Design CCW survey instrument grounded in students’ lived experiences, instructor feedback, and evidence of validity. The broader goal is to help engineering educators recognize, value, and support the forms of knowledge, experience, and community-based resources students bring to design work.
This is a full-time postdoctoral research scholar position. The anticipated start date is late Fall 2026 or early Spring 2027. The appointment is for up to 2 years contingent on funding, performance, and project needs. Salary will be commensurate with experience and ASU guidelines.
Essential Functions
The postdoctoral research scholar will:
• Support qualitative analysis of student interview data related to Community Cultural Wealth in engineering design courses.
• Support recruitment and data collection with engineering students and engineering design instructors.
• Contribute to the development of instructor-facing vignettes based on student interview data.
• Analyze qualitative data from instructor interviews and student cognitive interviews.
• Assist with translating qualitative findings into construct definitions and survey items for the Design CCW instrument.
• Help design and refine cognitive interview and card sorting protocols for gathering validity evidence.
• Lead and co-author journal manuscripts, conference papers, research-to-practice publications, and project reports.
• Contribute to dissemination activities, including workshops, an open-source scale manual, implementation guidelines, and resources for responsible use of the instrument.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor - Immunology
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: School of Life Sciences
jobs.description:
The School of Life Sciences (SOLS) invites applications for a full-time, benefits-eligible, non-tenure-eligible Assistant Teaching Professor position with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027. The position is 80% teaching and 20% service. Subsequent academic year renewals (Aug. 16 to May 15) are contingent upon satisfactory performance, availability of resources, and the needs of the unit. Supplementary summer teaching may be available. This position is located on the Tempe Campus in Tempe, Arizona and requires physical presence at that location.
Applicants should have advanced knowledge of immunology, as well as experience in teaching and mentoring at the college or university level. Ideally, candidates will also have research experience in immunology or a related field.
Successful applicants will contribute to SOLS’ innovative online and im person BS and MS programs in biology with focus on the area of immunology. They will be responsible for developing and providing instruction in Master’s-level and undergraduate courses in immunology and related topics. This includes supervising coursework for Applied Projects and Capstones for the Biology MS program. Responsibilities will include supervising graduate teaching assistants and updating/developing course materials with other faculty & staff. This person will also provide service within the school, college, and university in capacities appropriate for the position.
About School of Life Sciences
With more than 100 full-time faculty members and excellent undergraduate and graduate training programs, the School of Life Sciences (SOLS) (https://sols.asu.edu/about/mission-vision) has wide-ranging expertise across the biological sciences. SOLS supports and encourages multiple interdisciplinary research initiatives. The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and SOLS value our cultural and intellectual breadth and continually strive to foster a welcoming and inclusive environment. ASU’s stimulating and highly collaborative environment provides access to state-of-the-art equipment and core facilities.
About The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of Arizona State University, committed to improving communities on a local, national, and global scale. We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large, curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.
About Arizona State University
ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural, and overall health of the communities it serves.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Physics (R0008837)
jobs.institution: Wake Forest University: Physics
jobs.description:
WAKE FOREST UNIVERSITY. The Department of Physics invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Physics that will start July 1, 2027.
Qualifications: A Ph.D. in Physics or a closely related field is required for the position. Qualified applicants will demonstrate their ability to teach physics courses, initiate and sustain original research and scholarship in biophysics and/or materials science, and contribute to an academic environment that fosters learning and growth for all its stakeholders. We are particularly interested in candidates conducting experimental research in biophotonics, biomaterials, or bioelectronics and in candidates pursuing AI-focused research in biophysics or materials science using computational and/or experimental approaches. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to benefit from extensive facilities (physics.wfu.edu/research/facilities) including new state-of-the-art equipment obtained through recent university investments. Ideally, the successful candidate will work at the intersection between materials science and biophysics and will strengthen the connections between those groups.
Position Summary: This individual will be expected to teach physics courses at the graduate and undergraduate level, engage in scholarly activities, participate in departmental, College, and University service, and contribute to the University’s community outreach efforts. In keeping with the Teacher-Scholar model practiced at Wake Forest University, the successful candidate will establish a vigorous, externally supported research program and create a learning environment that welcomes all students into scientific study and supports their ongoing success. Candidates whose research interests complement those of current Wake Forest Physics faculty are particularly encouraged to apply, as we seek to increase opportunities for collaborative research.
About the Department of Physics: The department offers BA, BS, MS, and PhD degrees in Physics, an MS and certificate in Quantum Information Sciences, and a BS in Biophysics. The department emphasizes interdisciplinary study and close student-faculty collaboration. Opportunities for multidisciplinary collaboration include the Center for Functional Materials (cfm.wfu.edu), the Nano and Quantum Technologies Laboratory (wake-nanotech.org), the Translational Science Center (tsc.wfu.edu), the Center for Molecular Signaling (molecularsignaling.wfu.edu), and the other centers at the university (provost.wfu.edu/centers-institutes), as well as collaborations with faculty at the Wake Forest University School of Medicine. Additional information about the department is available at physics.wfu.edu.
About Wake Forest University: Founded in 1834, Wake Forest University is a private, coeducational institution dedicated to academic excellence in liberal arts, graduate, and professional education. With more than 5,400 undergraduates and 3,800 graduate and professional students, Wake Forest is a collegiate university offering a vibrant, intellectual community with a rich cultural life, an impressive array of facilities, and a strong athletics program competing in the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC). Since its founding, the University has adopted the motto Pro Humanitate, which is exemplified by a deep institutional commitment to public service and engagement with the world. For more information, visit: about.wfu.edu.
Wake Forest University is located in Winston-Salem, a beautiful, mid-sized city in the Piedmont-Triad region of North Carolina. To learn more about Winston-Salem, visit: www.visitwinstonsalem.com.
Application Instructions: Review of applications will begin November 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. To ensure full consideration, applications should be submitted by November 15, 2026. The application package should include a cover letter explaining the candidate’s interest in joining the Wake Forest academic community and providing the names and contact information for at least three references; a curriculum vitae; a statement of research plans (maximum 5 pages); and a statement of teaching philosophy (maximum 3 pages). To apply, visit: hr.wfu.edu/careers/. Questions about the search may be directed to the chair of the search committee Dr. Keith Bonin at bonin@wfu.edu or to Wake Forest University Human Resources at askhr@wfu.edu. Wake Forest University conducts background investigations for all final faculty candidates being considered for employment.

jobs.title: Open-Rank Professor of Chemical Engineering with a Specialization in Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.institution: Lehigh University: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering invites applications for an open-rank (Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) position with a specialization in biotechnology or biomolecular engineering, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. Tenure on hire is possible for senior candidates. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, next-generation bioprocess engineering, advanced drug delivery platforms, cellular and metabolic engineering, and the manufacturing of novel therapeutic modalities, including cell and gene therapies, mRNA therapeutics, and complex biologics. They will bring a compelling vision for advancing nursing science and interdisciplinary scholarship, along with a demonstrated ability to foster collaboration across Columbia University, Columbia University Irving Medical Center, and external partners. The Vice Dean will champion innovative research that addresses pressing health challenges, informs policy and practice, and translates scientific discovery into meaningful improvements in health outcomes.
COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF NURSING
The Columbia University School of Nursing (Columbia Nursing) is one of the nation's leading schools of nursing and a recognized innovator in nursing education, research, clinical practice, and health policy. Founded in 1892, the School is among the oldest nursing schools in the United States and has played a pioneering role in shaping the nursing profession, including establishing the nation's first clinical nursing specialty master's degree program and the first university-based midwifery program. Today, Columbia Nursing advances its mission through world-class education, groundbreaking research, and clinical innovation aimed at improving health outcomes and advancing health equity locally and globally.
Situated within Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC) in Washington Heights, the School benefits from close collaboration with the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, the Mailman School of Public Health, the College of Dental Medicine, NewYork-Presbyterian, and a broad network of academic, clinical, and community partners. Columbia Nursing's location within one of the world's premier academic health centers creates exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary scholarship, education, and clinical care.
Columbia Nursing offers a comprehensive portfolio of graduate and professional programs, including the Master's Direct Entry (MDE) program, Master of Science in Advanced Clinical Management and Leadership, Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP), Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Online Prerequisites for Entry to Nursing (OPEN) program, and subspecialty programs in Oncology and Women's Health. With more than 600 students enrolled across its graduate degree programs, the School prepares future clinicians, scientists, educators, and healthcare leaders through rigorous academic training grounded in scientific inquiry, innovation, and clinical excellence.
With 68 full-time faculty members, alongside part-time, attending, and clinical preceptor staff, the School is home to an accomplished faculty of scholars, clinicians, and innovators whose work spans nursing science, health informatics, healthcare delivery, health policy, community and population health, implementation science, and clinical research. Columbia Nursing faculty include members of the National Academy of Medicine, Fellows of the American Academy of Nursing, Fellows of the New York Academy of Medicine, and other nationally and internationally recognized leaders whose scholarship continues to shape healthcare practice, policy, and education.
Research
Research is a defining strength of the Columbia University School of Nursing and a central pillar of its mission to advance health for all. Columbia Nursing has earned international recognition for innovative, rigorous scholarship and currently ranks among the nation's leading recipients of National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding among schools of nursing, including ranking first nationally in NIH funding for three consecutive years. Faculty, postdoctoral fellows, and students also secure support from a broad range of federal agencies, foundations, and healthcare organizations, reflecting the depth and impact of the School's research enterprise.
Integrated within Columbia University and Columbia University Irving Medical Center, Columbia Nursing's research enterprise is distinguished by its interdisciplinary approach and its commitment to translating scientific discovery into meaningful improvements in health and healthcare. Faculty collaborate across academic, clinical, and community settings to address complex challenges facing individuals, families, communities, and health systems in the United States and around the world.
The School's research portfolio spans a broad range of scientific disciplines and methodologies, including artificial intelligence, biobehavioral and omics research, data science and informatics, healthcare delivery innovation, primary and comprehensive care, symptom science, patient safety and quality, palliative care, prevention science, urban and global health, and research focused on underserved and vulnerable populations. A hallmark of Columbia Nursing's scholarship is its commitment to understanding and addressing the biological, social, behavioral, and structural factors that shape health outcomes and healthcare access.
Research centers and programs serve as hubs for innovation and collaboration across the School. These include the Center for Health Policy, the Center for Community-Engaged Health Informatics and Data Science, the Center for Healthcare Delivery Research and Innovations, the Center for Research on People of Color, and the Center for Sexual and Gender Minority Health Research. Together, these centers advance discovery, support interdisciplinary partnerships, and generate knowledge that informs policy, improves care delivery, and promotes health and well-being across diverse populations. Building on this strong foundation, the next Vice Dean of Research and Scholarship will have the opportunity to further elevate Columbia Nursing's national and global influence in nursing science, healthcare innovation, and research excellence.

jobs.title: Research Associate

jobs.description:
POSITION OBJECTIVE
The Department of Medicine, Division of Rheumatology, seeks a highly motivated and experienced Research Associate to support and advance clinical and translational research programs in rheumatology. The Research Associate will work closely with the Principal Investigator (PI) and multidisciplinary research teams to design, conduct, analyze, and disseminate clinical research focused on rheumatologic diseases.
The position requires a strong background in rheumatology, clinical research methodology, and statistical analysis. The Research Associate will independently manage assigned research projects from study development through data analysis, abstract and manuscript preparation, presentation, and dissemination. The individual will use statistical methods and software, including IBM SPSS Statistics, to analyze clinical research data and generate publication-quality tables and figures.
Under the direction of the PI, the Research Associate will contribute to the development of new research questions, study designs, analytical strategies, and collaborative research initiatives. The Research Associate will communicate regularly with the PI and collaborating departments, provide recommendations regarding study design and analytical methodology, and ensure that research projects progress efficiently and are completed according to established timelines.
The Research Associate will also contribute to scientific presentations, peer-reviewed publications, and grant applications, including the development of preliminary data and research materials to support new funding opportunities. The position requires a high level of scientific integrity, attention to detail, independence, collaboration, and commitment to responsible conduct of research.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
1. Plan, conduct, and interpret statistical analyses for clinical and translational research projects developed by the PI. Participate in the design and implementation of new studies and, when appropriate, independently develop research questions, experiments, and analytical approaches in collaboration with the PI. Manage assigned research projects from study initiation through data analysis and dissemination. Monitor project progress, identify potential challenges or barriers, and provide regular updates and recommendations to the PI. Collaborate with faculty, research staff, bioinformatics personnel, and other departments to facilitate study completion. Interpret research findings and provide scientifically sound recommendations regarding study design, statistical methodology, and analytical strategies. Ensure that research activities are conducted with scientific rigor, accuracy, and adherence to institutional policies and responsible conduct of research. (30%)
2. Assist the PI in developing novel areas of clinical and translational research within rheumatology. Independently identify opportunities for new research questions, hypotheses, and analytical approaches. Apply appropriate statistical methods to clinical research datasets using IBM SPSS Statistics and other analytical tools as needed. Collaborate with investigators and research teams to develop innovative approaches to clinical research. Contribute to database development, data management, quality control, and interpretation of complex clinical datasets. Evaluate and recommend appropriate analytical methodologies based on the research question, study design, and available data. (30%)
3. Prepare abstracts for submission to national and international rheumatology and scientific meetings. Present research findings at departmental research meetings, scientific conferences, seminars, and other academic forums. Prepare manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed scientific journals. Develop publication-quality tables, figures, and other research materials. Contribute to grant applications through development and analysis of preliminary data, research summaries, figures, and other supporting materials. Collaborate with the PI and other investigators in communicating research findings to scientific and clinical audiences. (20%)
4. Independently develop and execute research projects under the overall guidance of the PI. Assemble, clean, analyze, and interpret research data. Generate publication-quality figures, tables, and statistical outputs. Serve as first author or co-author on manuscripts resulting from research conducted within the research program. Contribute to study protocols, research reports, abstracts, manuscripts, presentations, and grant proposals. Maintain the highest standards of scientific integrity, research ethics, data accuracy, confidentiality, and responsible conduct of research. Take ownership of assigned projects and ensure timely completion of research milestones and deliverables. (15%)
NONESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
1. Perform other research related duties and responsibilities as assigned by the PI or Department. (3%)
2. Participate in departmental and institutional research initiatives as appropriate. (2%)
CONTACTS
Department: Frequent interaction with the PI and rheumatology faculty. Regular collaboration with research coordinators, research staff, administrative personnel, and other members of the clinical research team. Collaboration with faculty investigators involved in multidisciplinary research projects.
University: Regular or occasional interaction with investigators and staff from other departments and academic units. Collaboration with the Bioinformatics and Biostatistics teams as appropriate. Communication with other University departments and research resources required for successful completion of research projects.
External: Supply vendors, other institutions, funding agencies, etc. as needed
Students: Undergraduate and graduate student employees working in the lab
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY
No direct supervisory responsibilities. The Research Associate may provide scientific guidance, training, and project-level directions to research staff and trainees as appropriate.
QUALIFICATIONS
Education/Experience: Medical degree (MD or DO) or PhD or master’s in clinical research. Clinical research experience in rheumatology preferred. Demonstrated experience in clinical research design, data analysis, scientific writing, and research dissemination. Minimum 5 years of experience developing abstracts, manuscripts, scientific presentations, and/or grant materials strongly preferred.
REQUIRED SKILLS
Statistical Analysis: Demonstrated proficiency in IBM SPSS Statistics and application of statistical methods to clinical research data.
Research Methodology: Strong understanding of clinical research methodology, study design, data interpretation, and analytical approaches.
Scientific Writing: Demonstrated ability to prepare scientific abstracts, manuscripts, research reports, and presentations.
Analytical Skills: Excellent ability to evaluate complex datasets, interpret findings, formulate conclusions, and provide scientifically appropriate recommendations.
Communication: Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with physicians, researchers, research staff, administrative personnel, and external collaborators.
Organization and Project Management: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize competing responsibilities, meet deadlines, and maintain accurate records.
Attention to Detail: Demonstrated commitment to accuracy, quality control, reproducibility, and timely completion of research activities.
Leadership and Collaboration: Ability to lead research activities, work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, provide guidance to research staff, and foster productive working relationships.
Independence and Initiative: Ability to work independently, take ownership of assigned projects, identify problems, develop solutions, and function effectively with appropriate guidance from the PI.
Problem Solving and Innovation: Strong critical-thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to develop creative and scientifically rigorous approaches to research questions.
Data and Technology: Strong computer skills, including database management and the ability to learn and utilize new research and analytical software as needed.
Multilingual Skills: Ability to communicate in multiple languages is strongly preferred and may be beneficial in clinical research involving diverse patient populations.
WORKING CONDITIONS
The Research Associate will primarily work in an indoor office and research environment. The position may occasionally require accompanying the PI during clinical activities or participating in research-related activities involving patients.
The position will generally follow standard first-shift business hours, with occasional hybrid work arrangements and evening or weekend activities as required by research protocols, scientific meetings, project deadlines, or the discretion of the PI.
The position requires flexibility, responsiveness, and the ability to adapt to changing research priorities, project timelines, and departmental needs.
Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary for this position at the time of its posting. The starting annual salary is $55,000-$70,000, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.
Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.

jobs.title: The Harlem Chair for the Study of History and Culture

jobs.description:
The Bard Prison Initiative (BPI) invites applications of distinguished scholars for an endowed, full-time faculty position, the Harlem Chair for the Study of History and Culture. This faculty member will be the professor-in-residence at the Bard Microcollege for Just Community Leadership, located in Harlem, New York. A Ph.D. in history, American studies, art history, anthropology, sociology, or a related field is expected. Strong candidates will have a combination of the following: a strong record of scholarly research and publication or artistic or literary production, a record of public facing intellectual work that is proximate to the Harlem community, and a record as distinguished teacher of diverse student populations in discussion-based seminars. This two-year position starts July 1, 2027 with teaching responsibilities beginning in the fall semester. Review of applications to begin January 8, 2027.
The Chair will teach across the NYC Microcollege network and provide academic advising to students in Harlem. They will teach a 2-2 courseload, including writing intensive courses and one or more courses specifically focused on Harlem’s extraordinary past and present. Additional responsibilities include organizing and participating in public lectures, collaborating with staff on student and student and community engagement, and creating connections between the Microcollege and collections of local libraries, cultural institutions and other humanistic resources. Candidates with connections to Harlem community and community institutions are particularly encouraged to apply.
Successful candidates will be committed to innovative undergraduate teaching at a liberal arts college with a diverse student body; excel at working in a community that is broadly diverse with regard to race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, gender, nationality, sexual orientation and religion; maintain an active research program; and be excited by rigorous, discussion-heavy and writing-based courses that center inclusive pedagogy and demand active participation of all students.
Created in partnership with local institutions, the Bard Microcolleges serve communities often excluded from the university experience. Students enroll in full-time, in-person, seminar-style courses culminating in Bard College associate in arts degrees. Scholarships cover tuition and fees, and books are provided. The Bard Microcollege in Harlem is a partnership among JustLeadershipUSA, College & Community Fellowship, and the Bard Prison Initiative. A curriculum dedicated to advocacy, arts, and sciences provides the community leaders of tomorrow with a broad education that is classical and contemporary, artistic and practical, global and local.
Consideration will be given to candidates who bring considerable experience and expertise to the position but who cannot commit to a two-year or full-time position. In this situation, salary is prorated and benefits eligibility depends on teaching load.
About BPI
Formed in 1999 to address the mass incarceration crisis, the Bard Prison Initiative (BPI) defies expectations of who college is for and where it might lead. For over twenty years, BPI has reimagined and redefined questions of availability, affordability, and expectations typically associated with college in America. One of the most rigorous and effective college-in-prison programs in the country, BPI is now extending its radical intervention in educational inequity outside of prison through the Bard Microcolleges and BardBac. BPI currently enrolls nearly 600 students across eleven campuses.

jobs.description:
The School of the Museum of Fine Arts at Tufts University seeks a full-time Professor of the Practice in Ceramics to begin September 1, 2027. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate studio courses in Ceramics, with particular strength in areas such as moldmaking, slip-casting, modular production, and/or expanded ceramic processes. Their practice may incorporate digital tools — including CAD modeling and 3D ceramic printing — as part of a sustained inquiry into material translation, repetition, scale, labor, and production, rather than as isolated technical competencies.
SMFA provides dedicated ceramics studio staffing and technical support. This position is focused on teaching, research and creative practice, curriculum development, and graduate and undergraduate mentorship, rather than studio operations or infrastructure management.
About SMFA
The School of the Museum of Fine Arts (SMFA) is a school within Tufts University’s School of Arts and Sciences. SMFA grants the BFA, MFA and MA degrees; students do not major in a single studio practice or area. SMFA faculty are practicing artists and researchers, and sustaining an active creative and research practice — alongside teaching — is an ongoing expectation of the role. Candidates should understand this structure and be prepared to envision their teaching, research, and creative practice within it.
What We’re Looking For
We seek an artist-educator whose practice is grounded in ceramics as a discipline and whose research and teaching engage mold-based, serial, and/or digitally mediated material processes as a central methodological and conceptual focus. The successful candidate will demonstrate a significant record of professional achievement and maintain an active creative and research practice that situates ceramics within contemporary conversations in art, design, and material culture.
The successful candidate will bring broad knowledge of ceramic materials, processes, and histories, with the ability to teach foundational skills and support advanced and graduate inquiry across diverse approaches to ceramic practice.
This position is envisioned as a collaborative appointment that strengthens disciplinary depth in Ceramics while connecting, through shared material processes and critical questions, with Sculpture, Installation, and related spatial practices. Working with Ceramics faculty, the successful candidate will contribute to curriculum development and shared mentorship of undergraduate and graduate students, while maintaining clear curricular boundaries and sustainable administrative structures.
While this search seeks a colleague with specific disciplinary expertise, SMFA’s programs and degrees are grounded in a broader institutional commitment to interdisciplinarity. We are looking for someone who will bring depth in their own practice while actively supporting students whose work moves across media and disciplines — and who can envision how their own teaching, research, and practice fit within SMFA’s cross-disciplinary structure.
We are also looking for a colleague with experience and interest in academic leadership. Relevant experience might include service as a department chair, director of graduate studies, or leadership of curricular or governance work.
We particularly welcome candidates whose work and teaching engage diverse cultural perspectives, expand the conceptual and material boundaries of ceramic practice, and support students from a wide range of backgrounds and educational pathways.

jobs.description:
The Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health is seeking applications and nominations for the position of Anna Cheskis Gelman and Murray Charles Gelman Professor and Chair of Epidemiology. The ideal candidate will have a national and global reputation as a top scientist, a leader in epidemiology, a distinguished educator, and a proven administrator and manager. This individual will possess a deep commitment to producing world-class science with real-world impact and training the next generation of epidemiology leaders in research and practice.
Reporting directly to the Dean of the School and serving as a key member of the School’s leadership team, the Chair will set a forward-looking and innovative vision for the Department of Epidemiology, leveraging its historic strengths and pioneering research to address contemporary challenges in public health while at the same time working to prepare and adapt to the future of the field and the scientific and practical needs of the public. The Chair will play a primary role in supporting and expanding a dynamic faculty, many of whom are recognized as leaders or emerging leaders in epidemiology and related fields. This role will also involve fostering innovative educational programs that prepare students to navigate and lead in the intricate landscape of science, public and community health, healthcare, government, and industry. The successful candidate will have a proven track record of academic achievement and reputation, substantial extramural grant support, and significant impact within public health. They will bring expertise in addressing both current and emerging challenges in epidemiology, a clear vision for future advancements, and the ability to quickly cultivate new partnerships. Demonstrable leadership and management capabilities also are essential.
DEPARTMENT OF EPIDEMIOLOGY
Columbia’s Department of Epidemiology is committed to producing world-class science with real-world impact while training the next generation of epidemiology leaders. As one of the oldest and largest departments of its kind, its scientists, teachers, and trainees address major public health challenges including infectious diseases and pandemics, cancer and chronic disease, gun violence and injury, opioid and substance use, mental health, aging, and the social and environmental conditions that shape health and longevity.
The Department includes 53 full-time faculty and 52 part-time affiliate and adjunct faculty, for a total of 105 faculty in these categories. It also includes approximately 300 employees across faculty, administrative, and research roles, including primary full-time, primary part-time, secondary, and jointly appointed faculty. Department faculty include elected members of the U.S. National Academy of Medicine, fellows of the Royal Society, Lasker Award recipients, and members of the American Epidemiological Society.
The Department has a substantial sponsored-research enterprise, with direct financial responsibility for more than 100 extramurally funded projects. Department faculty publish nearly 1,000 scholarly articles each year and conduct research through a worldwide network spanning more than 60 countries. Their work has informed public policy, clinical and public health practice, national and international guidance, and scientific discourse.
A defining feature of the Department is its extensive collaboration across Columbia University. Faculty hold joint appointments and work closely with departments throughout the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, as well as the New York State Psychiatric Institute, the Gertrude H. Sergievsky Center, the Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center, Columbia Law School, Teachers College, Columbia Engineering, the School of Social Work, Columbia Global Centers, and other University units. Faculty and graduates also maintain strong connections with the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, the New York State Department of Health, and public health agencies around the nation and the world.
ROLE OF THE CHAIR
The next Chair of the Department of Epidemiology will have the opportunity to lead a large, highly accomplished, and globally connected department at a time of rapid change in science, public health, higher education, and research funding. The Chair will provide strategic, academic, and administrative leadership for a department whose faculty, students, staff, and programs contribute to public health knowledge and practice locally, nationally, and globally.
As the Department’s academic leader, the Chair will set and advance a compelling vision for the future of epidemiology at Columbia. The Chair will support and develop outstanding faculty, strengthen the research enterprise, promote innovation in education and training, foster a collaborative and inclusive departmental culture, and ensure that students and trainees receive rigorous preparation for leadership in research and practice. The Chair will oversee departmental operations and resources, including budgets, sponsored research, personnel, space, and strategic investments, while ensuring compliance with institutional and funding requirements.
The Chair will recruit, retain, mentor, and develop faculty and staff; provide leadership and oversight for faculty advancement and promotion processes, including supporting early-stage investigators and guiding faculty progressing from Associate Professor to Full Professor; support principal investigators in securing competitive funding; strengthen interdisciplinary and interprofessional activities across Columbia; and cultivate partnerships with public agencies, communities, funders, alumni, and external organizations. Given the size and career-stage composition of the Department, the Chair will play an important role in ensuring that faculty receive appropriate mentorship, guidance, and support throughout the promotion process.
KEY OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES FOR THE NEXT CHAIR
Define the next chapter of epidemiologic science.
The Department’s breadth creates an opportunity for the next Chair to articulate a forward-looking scientific vision that builds on longstanding strengths while anticipating emerging public health needs, new methodologies, evolving data environments, and opportunities for intervention and implementation. The Chair will help connect scientific discovery with application and ensure that the Department remains responsive to changing health challenges locally and globally.
Strengthen interdisciplinary and cross-institutional collaboration.
Epidemiology faculty are deeply connected across Columbia University, CUIMC, public agencies, research centers, and global partners. The next Chair will have the opportunity to deepen these relationships, create new interdisciplinary partnerships, and strengthen translational research and training that bridge population health, clinical care, policy, community engagement, and implementation.
Sustain and diversify the research enterprise.
The Department manages a large and complex portfolio of externally funded research. In an evolving funding environment, the next Chair will support faculty success in securing competitive federal funding while identifying opportunities with foundations, philanthropy, industry, and other mission-aligned partners. The Chair will be expected to steward resources carefully, support innovation, and maintain a strong and sustainable operating position.
Advance excellence in education and training.
With 340 enrolled students across MPH, MS, online MS, DrPH, and PhD programs, as well as numerous doctoral and postdoctoral training initiatives, the Department has a substantial educational mission. The next Chair will support curricular innovation, rigorous methodological training, strong mentorship, and pathways that prepare graduates to lead across academia, public health practice, healthcare, government, industry, and community settings.
Recruit, develop, and support an exceptional faculty and staff community.
The next Chair will play a central role in recruiting, mentoring, developing, and retaining outstanding faculty and staff while fostering a culture of collaboration, inclusion, transparency, intellectual curiosity, and academic excellence. The Chair will support faculty across career stages, strengthen leadership development, provide clear feedback and expectations, and ensure that the Department’s people and organizational structures are positioned for continued success.
